anomalies.observed: R3 (10K) pulls NET0006, connected to PB4 on both MCU options (U4.3 and U2.3), up to VCC. The MCUs are powered from +5V, while U3 takes VCC at its input and generates +5V at its output.
anomalies.expected: The PB4 pull-up should go to the MCU's +5V logic rail, or otherwise be limited so NET0006 cannot exceed the MCU's supply voltage. Pulling it to the regulator input rail risks overvoltage if VCC is above the MCU's permitted input range.

evidence.quote: R3 10K; VCC; NET0006; U4 XTAL2/PB4; U2 PB4; U3 VI VCC, VO +5V (sheet /, page 1)

anomalies.impact: If VCC is above the +5V MCU rail, the pull-up can drive PB4 above the MCU's safe input voltage, potentially causing unreliable operation or damaging the MCU.

parsed.summary: R3 pulls the shared PB4 net to VCC rather than the +5V rail powering the ATtiny options. Since VCC is also the input to the 5V regulator, an input supply above the MCU rail can overvoltage PB4.
